description: A single-panel figure that is entirely a data table (no micrographs, spectra or curves), rendering the quantitative characterisation of four rolled specimens. The header row reads: Specimen | HAGBs [%] | GOS≤2° [%] | Dislocation density [m⁻²] | C/F [GPa] | M [GPa] | F [GPa] | DIF [GPa]. Four specimen rows are given: R650 (49.6, 12.3, 3.9 × 10¹⁴, C/F 3.6 ± 0.6, F 2.9 ± 0.3), R750 (43.5, 6.9, 3.4 × 10¹⁴, C/F 3.6 ± 0.5, F 2.9 ± 0.2), R850 (60.1, 19.4, 2.1 × 10¹⁴, M 6.0 ± 0.5, F 2.6 ± 0.3, DIF 3.0 ± 0.3) and R950 (75.7, 25.8, 2.8 × 10¹⁴, M 6.5 ± 0.5, F 2.8 ± 0.2, DIF 2.8 ± 0.4). Dashes ("–") occupy the C/F cells of R850 and R950 and the M and DIF cells of R650 and R750, i.e. those constituents are absent from those specimens. The table shows high-angle grain-boundary (HAGB) fraction rising from a minimum at R750 to a maximum at R950, dislocation density falling then rising between R650 and R950, GOS≤2° fraction tracking the HAGB trend, and nano-hardness of the individual constituents in GPa. The figure demonstrates that raising the rolling temperature to 950 °C increases both HAGB fraction and GOS≤2° fraction while transforming the hard constituent from C/F (carbide/ferrite) to martensite and DIF.

observations.observation: The figure is a single tabular panel with columns Specimen, HAGBs [%], GOS≤2° [%], Dislocation density [m⁻²], C/F [GPa], M [GPa], F [GPa], DIF [GPa].
HAGB fraction is 49.6% (R650), 43.5% (R750), 60.1% (R850) and 75.7% (R950), i.e. lowest at R750 and highest at R950.
Dislocation density is 3.9 × 10¹⁴ m⁻² (R650), 3.4 × 10¹⁴ m⁻² (R750), 2.1 × 10¹⁴ m⁻² (R850) and 2.8 × 10¹⁴ m⁻² (R950).
C/F nano-hardness is 3.6 ± 0.6 GPa for R650 and 3.6 ± 0.5 GPa for R750; the C/F cell contains a dash for R850 and R950.
M nano-hardness is 6.0 ± 0.5 GPa for R850 and 6.5 ± 0.5 GPa for R950; the M cell contains a dash for R650 and R750.
DIF nano-hardness is 3.0 ± 0.3 GPa for R850 and 2.8 ± 0.4 GPa for R950; the DIF cell contains a dash for R650 and R750.

The caption states the figure reports the proportion of HAGBs, KAM values, grain sizes and nano-hardness of the tested steel, but the table image contains no KAM or grain-size column — only HAGB, GOS≤2°, dislocation density and four hardness columns.

The four specimens are labelled R650, R750, R850 and R950, consistent with the abstract's rolling-temperature range of 850–950 °C; the higher two temperatures were processed in that range while R650/R750 were not.
Both the HAGB fraction and the GOS≤2° fraction drop from R650 to R750 and then rise monotonically to R950, so the two quantities follow the same ranking across the four specimens.
The hard constituent changes with processing: only C/F is reported for R650 and R750, whereas M and DIF are reported only for R850 and R950.
